newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday March 19.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Italian Cabinet will meet this morning in order to discuss Albania's crisis and is expected to allow refugees a temporary residence permit of two months. Fleeing Albanians swelled to about 10,000 in five days, crowding the southern ports of Brindisi, Bari and Otranto. The government decided to repatriate 200 suspected criminals (all).

* A quarterly report on Italy's state accounts is expected to be published by the end of the week. The size of the planned mini-budget, which might be announced on March 27, will be based on the report's figures for the public deficit (all).

* The lira fell to a four month low of 1007 against the German mark, despite dealer reports of Bank of Italy intervention above 1003. The currency market was dominated by increasing worries about the launch of Europe's economic and monetary union following comments from Bundesbank council member Kuehbacher. He said an EMU delay would be the only option if Germany did not fulfil Maastricht criteria for EMU. The Italian stock market fell by 1.2 percent (all).

* A report by ISTAT, the national statistics institute, showed provisional figures for Italy's industrial production in January, with industrial output down 6.4 percent year-on-year but up 0.4 percent month-on month (all).
* Italian state-controlled energy group ENI said its preliminary consolidated net profit for 1996 grew nearly 3 percent on the previous year to 4.45 trillion lire (all).

* A controlling stake in Italy's largest publishing group Mondadori will be tranferred from SBHE, a Silvio Berlusconi personal company, to his financial holding company Fininvest. The stake of 60 million ordinary shares corresponds to 47.38 percent in Mondadori, price per share is settled at 12,500 lire (all).
* Giovanni Bazoli, chairman of Italian bank Banco Ambrosiano Veneto, said the group will make a capital issue of "major dimensions" by the end of this year (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
